I have resolved the issue in [django/db/models/sql/compiler.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-1b8eku27/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1407-L1413).

### Cause
When `Model.objects.all().delete()` (or any fast-deleted `QuerySet` without active table references in `alias_refcount`) is executed, [`SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-1b8eku27/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1409-L1412) checked the number of active aliases before the base table alias was initialized on `self.query`. Because `alias_map` was empty (or had zero reference counts), `single_alias` evaluated to `False` (`0 == 1`), causing [`SQLDeleteCompiler.as_sql()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-1b8eku27/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1423-L1440) to fall back to generating a `WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM ...)` subquery instead of a direct `DELETE FROM ...` statement.

### Solution
Updated [`SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-1b8eku27/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1409-L1412) to call [`self.query.get_initial_alias()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-1b8eku27/django/db/models/sql/query.py#L916-L926) first to ensure the base table is present and referenced in the query before counting active aliases.
